# Report — round 001 (L1 proxy, CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline)

Representation: L1 proxy. Single continuous first-person shot (no cuts) at 1280x720, 60 fps, 402 frames, 6.7 s; update(time) is absolute.

Geometry: box/cylinder proxies for the bombsite floor, site-edge ledge, right low wall with two baskets, stairs to an upper platform, a tall wooden crate stack at the start, three standing cement sacks plus a lying sack, four white crates with teal tarp tops (front crate Q, left P, right R, rear S), a red bombsite ring/X floor marking, a sloped ramp/street to the left with sidewalks, curbs, a parked car, a utility pole and a small star crate, a diagonal tan building with windows, white buildings with shutters, the far sign building, and seeded skyline boxes.

Characters: articulated proxy humanoids (hip, torso, head, two legs, two arms). An enemy walks up the ramp, is shot at 2.82 s and falls backward to lie on the street (gun drops); a second player stands on a block at the right (visible only during the early right look); an earlier casualty lies near the car.

Viewmodel: purple AWP proxy (stock, barrel, scope with yellow band, green glove and forearm) attached to the camera. It is swapped for a green-glove knife between about 1.0 and 1.6 s, and has a recoil kick, muzzle flash and tracer at the shot.

Camera: hand-keyframed Hermite track for position, yaw, pitch and eye height. It starts behind the crate, looks right briefly (0.28 s), walks forward past the sacks, looks right at the crates (1.75-2.0 s), flicks left and then aims at the enemy (2.3-2.9 s), approaches the front crate (3.2-3.8 s) and slips left between the crates (4.07 s). It then strafes left toward the ledge (4.4-5.5 s), hops onto the ledge (about 5.6-5.9 s) and drops onto the ramp sidewalk (6.1-6.7 s).

Observed vs inferred: poses at the 24 sample times are estimated from those images. The motion between samples, the exact layout, the distances, the shot time (between 2.62 and 2.90 s) and the enemy's path are inferred. HUD overlays are intentionally not reproduced.

Feedback: none received yet (initial scene). All positions are approximate and unverified.

rounds.reason: Re-laid out the bombsite and early camera path from round-001 feedback; thicker viewmodel and stronger recoil

# Report — round 002 (L1 proxy, CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline)

Representation: L1 proxy. Single continuous first-person shot (no cuts) at 1280x720, 60 fps, 402 frames, 6.7 s; update(time) is absolute.

Feedback received: round-001 render pairs for all 24 samples. The late street, ledge and crate segment roughly matched. The early and middle bombsite views did not: the tan windowed wall was far too distant, a near white building and the upper platform blocked the view toward the ramp, the wooden crate was too dark and short, and the AWP viewmodel was too thin. Recoil was barely visible.

Revisions in this round:
- Re-solved the early camera path and yaws. I used a small least-squares fit of the bearings of the tan wall, crates, sacks, stairs, wooden crate and sign building as seen in the samples (an offline helper script, not a scene render).
- Moved the tan building to the ramp top so it sits about 12 m from the shooting position, with the enemy standing in front of it.
- Moved the white building with the door and red shutters back onto the upper platform, behind the stairs.
- Rotated the right low wall with baskets so it runs diagonally to the second player's block.
- Made the crate stack lighter and taller, brightened the lighting and floor colours, and made the AWP stock, scope and glove much thicker.
- Made the recoil kick stronger.
- Moved the enemy's fall and body position so the body is visible on the ramp in the final frames, and moved the car and the second body to match the street views.

Geometry and characters are unchanged in kind: box/cylinder proxies for the site and props, and articulated proxy humanoids (the enemy walks, is shot at 2.82 s and falls backward; a second player stands on a block at the right; an earlier casualty lies near the car). The viewmodel is a purple AWP, swapped for a green-glove knife between 1.0 and 1.55 s, with a muzzle flash and tracer at the shot.

Observed vs inferred: only the 24 sample frames were observed. The motion between samples, the shot instant, the enemy's path and all metric distances are inferred. HUD overlays are not reproduced.

Remaining uncertainties: the exact map layout, the bearings in the early frames (residual errors of several degrees), and where the crates sit relative to the end-of-ledge view.

# Final report (L1 proxy, CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline)

Submitted scene: the round-008 render, which is the most recently rendered candidate.

## What the scene is
- Representation level L1, built for the CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline.
- One continuous first-person shot with no cuts, at 1280x720, 60 fps, 402 frames, 6.7 s.
- update(time) is absolute and deterministic. Procedural skyline boxes use a seeded generator.

## Geometry
Box, cylinder and plane proxies make up the scene:
- the bombsite floor and the site-edge ledge (low wall)
- the far low wall, and a diagonal right low wall with two baskets
- stairs up to a platform
- a tall wooden crate stack at the start
- three standing cement sacks and a lying sack
- four white crates with teal tarp tops: front crate Q, left P, right R, rear S
- the red bombsite ring and X on the floor
- a sloped ramp street with sidewalks, red curbs, a lane line, a parked car, a utility pole and a small star crate
- a tan lattice-topped building with three windows at the ramp top
- a white building with a green band, red shutters and a door
- the sign ("teleboutique") building and white buildings with blue shutters
- seeded skyline boxes

## Characters and articulation
- Proxy humanoids made of hips, torso, head, two legs and two pivoting arms.
- Enemy: walks up the ramp (legs swinging), turns toward the site, and is shot at 2.82 s. He falls backward over about 0.4 s with his arms flung out, drops his rifle, and lies on the ramp for the rest of the shot.
- A second player stands on a block at the right; he is visible only during the quick right look at about 0.28 s.
- An earlier casualty lies near the car.

## Viewmodel and shot
- Purple AWP proxy (stock, barrel, scope with yellow band, green glove and forearm), attached to the camera.
- It swaps to a green-glove knife from about 1.0 to 1.55 s.
- At the shot it has a recoil kick, a muzzle flash and a tracer.

## Camera and timing
Hand-keyed monotone-cubic track of position, yaw, pitch and eye height. Poses at the sample times were estimated from landmark bearings and apparent sizes, partly with an offline least-squares helper (not a render). Sequence:
- starts behind the crate stack and looks right at about 0.28 s
- walks past the sacks, then looks right at the crates (1.75-2.0 s)
- flicks left to the stairs and the tan building (2.32 s), aims and fires (2.6-2.9 s)
- approaches the front crate (3.2-3.8 s) and slips left between the crates (4.07 s)
- strafes left toward the ledge (4.4-5.5 s), hops onto the ledge (about 5.6-5.9 s), and drops onto the ramp sidewalk (6.1-6.7 s)

## Observed vs inferred
- Observed: only the 24 reference samples.
- Inferred: the motion between samples, the exact shot frame (between 2.62 and 2.90 s), the enemy's path, the fall timing and all metric distances.
- HUD overlays (minimap, scoreboard, kill feed, ammo) are intentionally not reproduced.

## Feedback used
I received render/reference pairs for rounds 001-008 and revised the scene after each:
- Round 2: re-laid out the bombsite and solved the early camera path.
- Round 3: fixed an eye-height interpolation overshoot that had made the camera dip far below eye level in the middle of the sequence.
- Rounds 4-7: rearranged the crate cluster and refit the poses during the approach and the shot.
- Round 8: re-placed the tan building, the enemy and his body, and refined the 2.32 s look.
- I did not inspect a render of the round-008 changes in detail beyond the 2.32, 2.9 and 4.65 s samples.

## Remaining discrepancies
- The tan building still sits several degrees left of the reference in the 2.3-2.9 s views, and is somewhat too prominent at the left edge at 6.1 s.
- Background building placement and distances are approximate.
- The early-frame bearings have residual errors of several degrees.
- The left crate looks slightly closer than in the reference at 4.4-5.2 s.
- The second player is posed simply; the fallen body is a rigid proxy pose.
- The knife model is a minimal proxy.
- None of this has been scored.
